title: Thread ledger: checkpoints and entries bound to a story

story.as_a: orchestrator or runner session working a delivery story
story.i_want_to: record each checkpoint and each reasoning, finding, fix and verdict entry against the story's thread
story.so_that: a reviewer and Mark read a change's reasoning next to its diff, in one place, without a pull request

rationale: loopctl holds everything around a change except the change; PRD §3.

acceptance_criteria.description: A thread_checkpoints table (tenant_id, story_id, seq, commit_sha, tree_sha, parent_checkpoint_id, kind checkpoint|base_update, claim_epoch, dispatch_id, merge_commit_sha, inserted_at) exists with RLS enabled, unique (story_id, commit_sha) and unique (story_id, seq).

A thread_entries table (tenant_id, story_id, seq, kind, author_principal, dispatch_id, idempotency_key NOT NULL, body, checkpoint_id, finding_ids, introduced_by, severity, inserted_at) exists with RLS enabled, unique (story_id, seq) and unique (story_id, author_principal, idempotency_key); kind is one of message, checkpoint, review_requested, finding, fix, verdict, escalation, merge.
Recording a checkpoint is refused with 409 stale_claim_epoch unless the caller is the story's current claimant and names the story's current claim_epoch; the checkpoint's seq is assigned server-side.
Re-sending an entry with the same idempotency_key from the same author returns the existing entry with 200 and writes nothing; the same key from a different author is a distinct entry.
Entry bodies are bounded by one module attribute that both the changeset and the OpenAPI operation reference, and a body over the bound is 422.

A finding entry must reference a checkpoint of the same story; a fix entry must name at least one finding of the same story; a finding recorded after the first completed review round without introduced_by is 422.
Every recorded checkpoint and entry appends an audit-chain event for the story.

GET /api/v1/stories/:id/thread returns the checkpoints and entries in seq order, with entry bodies marked untrusted; MCP tools thread_get, thread_checkpoint and thread_entry call the three endpoints, declared and dispatched, with a README row each.
Tenant B cannot read or write tenant A's thread.

test_cases.name: migrations create the tables with RLS
expected_results: tables and unique indexes present; RLS enabled

test_cases.name: checkpoint from a stale epoch is refused
steps: POST checkpoint with an old epoch

test_cases.name: idempotent entry
expected_results: one row; second answer 200 with the same id

test_cases.name: entry validation
steps: oversized body; finding without checkpoint; fix without finding; round-2 finding without introduced_by

test_cases.name: audit events
steps: record a checkpoint and an entry
expected_results: two audit events on the story

test_cases.name: read the thread and the MCP wiring
steps: GET thread; node test on tool declaration and dispatch
expected_results: seq order; untrusted marker; tools declared and dispatched

test_cases.name: tenant isolation
steps: tenant B reads and writes tenant A's thread

technical_notes: Never add tenant_id, story_id, seq or author_principal to a cast list. author_principal is derived from the authenticating key. The route coverage test in mcp-server must see the new routes reached.
